reason: The trigger sits 110 days before the row's date, outside the 90-day window: on 18 May 2026 InstaVolt announced £250m of committed debt financing from an oversubscribed lender consortium (Close Brothers, Investec, KfW IPEX-Bank, Lloyds, National Wealth Fund, NatWest, Rabobank, Santander, Société Générale) plus a £40m equity investment from owner EQT Infrastructure (Transport + Energy, BusinessGreen, InstaVolt newsroom). The recorded row understated it as 'funding size not stated'; the corrected figures do not change the verdict, and debt raised for charger and battery-storage capex is not a brand budget. The one in-window event is the agreed sale of the Spanish and Portuguese businesses to Powerdot (announced 1-2 Jul 2026, terms undisclosed) so that investment concentrates on the UK and Ireland: a divestment that narrows the footprint rather than a capital or identity inflection, leaving a UK-only network whose home stage (London E-Prix, Brands Hatch, May 2027) is a single-market activation. The battery-storage programme (five new sites, 20 more planned for 2026) is a £2.5m investment (Renewable Energy Magazine, 8 May 2026). Delvin Lane confirmed as CEO. No motorsport tie found; Jaguar TCS Racing's roster carries no charging-network partner, so the lane itself is open. Re-surface on a disclosed equity round, an IPO or sale process, or a UK partnership that brings a marketing budget.
